set.layering_notes: Madera County is a small non-entitlement county: the Community and Economic Development Department (planning, state CDBG and HOME applications) and Behavioral Health Services (BHSA, bridge housing) are the only County housing actors, the Housing Authority of the City of Madera (HACM) is the PHA for the county, and the Fresno Madera Continuum of Care (CA-514, led by Fresno County) handles HHAP and CoC funds. There is no County housing trust fund, NOFA, inclusionary ordinance or impact fee waiver program. The City of Madera is a separate CDBG and HOME entitlement with its own PLHA plan (Pass 3). maderacounty.com blocks automated access (403 on pages and documents), the PrimeGov and IQM2 portals returned no 2026 meetings, and Board agendas were read from PDFs mirrored on maderacountywater.com; other sources were HCD allocation tables, maderaha.org, zoneomics (County Code Title 18), CEQAnet and press coverage. The County's land use incentives are state minimums; the main 2026 development is the Housing Element rezoning around Madera Ranchos, Oakhurst and the Highway 99 corridor. Source is Chapter 18.114 text on zoneomics.com. Housing Element status: the County signed a CEQA Notice of Exemption (SCH 2025100344) on October 7, 2025 covering the 2024-2032 element, zoning text changes and rezones; HCD's Housing Element Compliance Report (data.ca.gov, updated November 6, 2026) shows the County's adopted 6th cycle housing element received October 20, 2025 and found in compliance December 16, 2025. HCD's September 9, 2025 letter said compliance required completing Programs 1.3 (by-right reuse of prior sites) and 1.4 (rezoning for the RHNA shortfall), so the rezones were adopted with the element. reason: Added HCD finding that the City's adopted element is out of compliance

set.layering_notes: Madera has no inclusionary ordinance or in-lieu fund. These fee tools are the only local cost reductions beyond HOME and PLHA. Program B-7 targets downtown revitalization, so it fits best for an affordable rental project downtown. Elsewhere, use the Director's waiver authority in MMC 10-8.17 and ask for a deferral under A-4. A fee waiver is a public subsidy and, depending on its size, can trigger state prevailing wage. The 6th Cycle Housing Element was adopted February 4, 2026, but HCD's Housing Element Compliance Report (updated November 6, 2026) shows the adopted element reviewed April 7, 2026 with compliance status Out. Until HCD finds it compliant, the City is exposed to the Builder's Remedy and cannot receive state funds that require a compliant element (PLHA, LHTF, IIG, AHSC). Madera County's density bonus (county record, Chapter 18.114) applies only in unincorporated areas.
